course.summary: The Indonesian national competency certification for work at height, aligned with Ministry of Manpower Regulation 9/2016 — a mandatory requirement on many domestic projects.
prerequisites: Senior high school education or equivalent
For Level 2: at least one year of documented work-at-height experience
National ID and a recent photograph
outcomes: Select, inspect, and correctly use fall-protection PPE
Install work restraint and fall arrest systems
Deliver rescue and evacuation of a casualty at height
Prepare work permits for work-at-height activities

syllabus.title: Day 1 — Regulation & Hazard Identification
syllabus.detail: Regulation 9/2016, Act 1/1970, hazard identification, risk assessment, and the hierarchy of control.

syllabus.title: Day 2 — PPE & Fall Protection Systems
syllabus.detail: Full body harnesses, energy-absorbing lanyards, anchorage, restraint systems, and fall clearance calculation.

syllabus.title: Day 3 — Practical & Rescue
syllabus.detail: Vertical ladder practice, platform work, rescue of a suspended casualty, and managing suspension trauma.

syllabus.title: Day 4 — BNSP Competency Assessment
syllabus.detail: Written, oral, and practical assessment by a BNSP-licensed assessor at a verified assessment venue.

course.certificate: BNSP Certificate of Competency and competency card, valid for 3 years, nationally registered.

sections.body:
## IRATA or BNSP — which one do you need?

Both are legitimate, but they answer different needs. BNSP is the national competency certification recognised by Indonesian regulators and is frequently an administrative requirement on government projects and for local contractors. IRATA is an international industry scheme that travels across borders and is typically demanded by multinational oil and gas operators.

Many of our technicians hold both. If you are unsure, send us your project details on WhatsApp and we will map the right certification with you.
